title: a valid `neural_block` descriptor is accepted by the shared validator but refused by every plugin-loading door
why: `neural_block` is a real, well-formed descriptor, so the shared validator
accepts it as structurally valid. But a descriptor only names other kernels
(a forward kernel and a VJP kernel) instead of containing runnable code, so
no loader that actually launches a kernel may accept it — each loader must
reject it with a message saying it is recognized but not launchable.
This fixture's JSON keys are ordered so that the nested `forward_exec.kernel`
key appears before the top-level `kernel` key. A validator that scans for
keys by text alone (rather than by JSON structure) could mistake the nested
kernel name for the descriptor's own identity; this fixture exercises that
exact confusion, so the key order must not be changed.
The descriptor carries no `aether_abi` (that tag belongs on the kernels it
references, not on the descriptor itself) and an empty `arg_spec` (present
but empty, since the parser requires the key to exist). The forward kernel's
companion VJP kernel is checked separately in the row01b fixture.
